classification: Reviewed actual complete-entry Gaussianization theorem and robust cross-norm gain; original all-orders convergence remains OPEN
conclusions: For actual complete sign B, d>=||B||op, m=n/d^2>=m_0>0 and epsilon=1-tr((B^T B)^2)/(n^2 d^2), beta(B)/(nd)>=kappa+(sqrt(kappa)-kappa)m-kappa epsilon-o_(m_0)(1), uniformly in B and d.
Exact flat nonzero singular values at d are equivalent to epsilon=0. Flat or asymptotically flat actual cross matrices with m bounded below have a strictly positive leading-order gain over kappa.

A self-contained uniform absolute-moment Gaussianization lemma handles delocalized sign coefficients and bounded Gaussian correlation operators. Mixed Hermite contractions, a characteristic-function equation, uniform integrability and an L2 tail argument supply the required bridge; variance alone is not used as an absolute-moment lower bound.

The actual pure-cross substitution requires p=q_A=0, c=Phi(K)=beta(B), and the separately given actual unweighted operator bound. No such operator bound follows here from diagonal dispersion or a diagonal trace cap.
The formal kappa-floor endpoint is excluded only in this actual scalar, bounded-operator setting. Weighted transfer, all-cell upper evaluation and original convergence are not concluded.
